To see where the time comes from, read 'show clock time-source': ntp means the NE synchronises from NTP, manual means it uses the NE internal clock. The default is manual. 'show clock' also gives current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, DST-active (true/false, default false) and last-time-jump, reported as '<time1> to <time2>' with jumps under 10 seconds ignored. If the DNS server is not properly configured, show clock can take up to 2 minutes to respond.

Yes. node-type is set with 'set ne node-type OADM'; permitted values are ILA, OADM and XPDR. It can only be set or changed on a 1830 GX G34c chassis, whose default is ILA (G31/G32 default OADM, G42 default XPDR); OADM on G34c is supported from R7.0 onward. To configure node-type OADM the guide requires that no OMS monitoring-mode in the system be 'ila-with-equalization' or 'not-monitored', that is no 'spectrum' (or 'ochm') objects exist in OADM, and that no direction-* exist. Going back the other way, to configure ILA, no OMS monitoring-mode on the dwdm-line ports may be 'intrusive' (no RD or PAx card can exist), and no degree, no oxcon and no nmc may exist. Note that G34c SLTE mode (l0-mode-op slte) is supported only when node-type is ILA, not when it is OADM.

'show ne-function' displays the Network Element generic functions in one listing. It is a show-only command with no parameters, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The output enumerates the node's direction and amplifier function objects together, for example on a 1830 GX G30 node: direction-1 through direction-8, amplifier-raman-1-7, amplifier-1-1-A, amplifier-1-1-B, amplifier-1-3.1-drop, amplifier-1-5-A, amplifier-1-5-B, amplifier-2-1-A, amplifier-2-1-B, amplifier-2-3-A, amplifier-2-3-B, and the ne-function entry itself.

Use the ntp command (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode): 'set ntp ntp-enabled true' turns on NTP (ntp-enabled is true by default), and 'set ntp ntp-auth-enabled true' requires the synchronisation to be authenticated (ntp-auth-enabled defaults to false). The ntp object is system managed and cannot be manually added or deleted. The third settable attribute is assignment-method, with values manual, dhcp or both, default both, which selects whether the system uses manually configured NTP values, DHCP supplied ones, or both. 'show ntp' returns ntp-enabled, ntp-auth-enabled, assignment-method and ntp-active-server (the currently active NTP server). Authentication also needs keys defined with 'add ntp-key-<key-id>' and bound to a server through the ntp-server auth-key-id attribute.

NTP authentication keys are managed with 'add ntp-key-<key-id> key-type <value> key-value <value> [is-trusted <value>]', with matching set, show and delete forms (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). key-type is the hash algorithm used for NTP message digest computation and accepts sha-1, aes-cmac, sha-256 and md5; there is no default. key-id is a number in the range 1..65534. key-value is a string of length 8 to 40 characters. is-trusted marks the key as a trusted NTP key and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Example: 'add ntp-key-2 is-trusted true key-type sha-1 key-value Infinera'.

Yes. The ntp-server origin attribute is exactly for this: a DHCP configured NTP entry is converted into a manually configured one by changing origin. Run 'set ntp-server-<ip-address> origin manual'. The permitted values are dhcp (address assigned to this system by a DHCP server) and manual (address manually configured); the default is manual. The server key is the IP address, and IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name are accepted. Other settable attributes on the same object are auth-key-id (uint32 or not-applicable, default not-applicable), label (0..256 characters), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed). 'show ntp-server-<ip-address>' additionally returns oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state.

Use 'show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>', for example 'show ntp-server-status-172.19.13.218' (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). The key field is reach: an 8-bit shift register of the recent probes with the most recent probe in the 2^0 position, where the value 377 indicates that all the recent probes have been answered. Alongside it you get when (seconds elapsed since the last packet was received), poll (polling interval in seconds), delay (path delay to the server in ms), offset (clock offset to the peer in ms), jitter (path jitter in ms), stratum of the remote peer, refid (reference clock type or address), type (local, unicast, multicast or broadcast), auth-status (ok, yes, bad or none, default none) and condition, whose possible values include sys.peer, reject and candidate.

'restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>]' (Operational Mode) takes type cold, warm or shutdown. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting; the system regains connectivity within five minutes (a cold reboot of an XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost, while cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting). warm reboots only the processor of the CHM6, UCM4 and similar and is non service affecting, again regaining connectivity within five minutes (on XMM4 it is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes). shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. If you do not supply <type>, a warm start is done by default. If you omit <resource-id>, the active node controller card is restarted. The command asks for confirmation unless -f is given, and not all cards support all restart types. Cards can be restarted cold, warm or shutdown, card sub-components cold or warm, and toms cold only.

'set-time' is only applicable when the time-source is manual, that is when NTP is not enabled. If the node is synchronising from NTP it will not accept a hand-set time; check with 'show clock time-source' (values ntp and manual, default manual) and disable synchronisation with 'set ntp ntp-enabled false' if you really need to set it by hand. The syntax is 'set-time [new-time=]<value>' in Operational Mode, with the value in a format derived from ISO 8601 combining date and time, for example 'set-time 2021-02-06T11:16:58Z' where Z is UTC, or a non-UTC offset as in 'set-time 2021-04-01T18:46:44+03:00'. Read the resulting time back with the 'time' command, which reports it in the system configured timezone rather than the timezone used on the set-time command.

Yes: 'status equipment' (Operational mode). The Equipment dashboard summarises all equipment in the system with the relevant details, including temperature sensors and power values, plus the list of chassis, the cards per chassis with their subtype, the toms per card, and generic status covering presence or absence, oper state and alarms. The default scope is the entire network element. On a large NE the output can be filtered per chassis by giving the chassis id as the filter, for example 'status equipment 5'; only existing chassis ids are accepted and wildcards are not supported, so you either get all chassis or exactly one. Output shows entries such as 'chassis-1 G42 (NC) ok/eqpt discovery temp 25C | power 2.1/4400 W' and fan speeds, with the tick, cross and padlock symbols marking oper-state enabled, oper-state disabled and admin-locked.

Use 'clear [-f] system [[action=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>]' in Operational Mode. type factory-reset resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing the respective files and user configurations, which may imply loss of connectivity; the clear is a secure wipe. The other types are full-wipe, which cleans the entire system and reinstalls software on the controller and line cards and needs a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover, and inactive, which clears the inactive software partition. target may be the whole system or a specific chassis or card AID; with no target the entire system is cleared. restart-behavior is a standard restart by default, or shutdown so the node does not come back up. Limits: factory-reset does not take effect for G30 Optical Carrier-Cards OCC2T and OCC2E, it is supported for the G30 controller card FRCU, and 'clear system factory-reset' with the shutdown option is not supported on L0 cards. For a simple database wipe use 'clear database' instead. Example: 'clear system factory-reset shutdown'.

Just type 'time'. It is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, takes no parameters, and prints the system's time in combined ISO 8601 date and time form, for example '2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00'. The time is reported using the system configured timezone. For more detail use 'show clock', which returns current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source, DST-active and last-time-jump, though note that if DNS is not properly configured show clock can take up to 2 minutes to return.

The 'uptime' command (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, no parameters) displays the system uptime and load average, for example '21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39'. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether multiple tasks are queued on the system or card. Whether a given number is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the card, and the load average number itself. The stated rule of thumb is that a load average value is considered high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card.

Yes. 'manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value>' (Operational mode) takes the AID of the object to be switched, and the command warns and asks you to confirm before proceeding: 'Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]'. Answer y at the prompt to proceed, or pass -f to force it without confirmation. The examples give 'manual-switchover card-1-3' on a 1830 GX G42 chassis, 'manual-switchover card-1-5' on a G32 chassis and 'manual-switchover card-1-12' on a G34c chassis. For the full procedure the guide points to the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

'show protection' displays the node's protection container. It is a show-only command with no parameters, available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the detail beneath it, use 'show protection-group-<name>' for the group attributes (protection-type, pg-state, pg-request, switching-mode, reversion-mode, hold-off-timer, wtr-timer, remaining-wtr, working-pu, protection-pu, reliable-cp and the switch triggers) and 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>' for each member's state and role.

On protection-group, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. The wait-to-restore timer is wtr-timer: the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, with a range of 60..720 seconds and a default of 300. It only applies in revertive mode, and reversion-mode itself takes revertive or non-revertive and defaults to non-revertive, so reversion is off unless you enable it. The related read-only remaining-wtr shows the time left on the WTR timer, range 0..720 seconds, again only applicable in revertive mode. The separate hold-off-timer, the switching trigger soaking time before switching, is set in 1-millisecond steps over the range 0..10000 ms and defaults to 0.

Use the operating command 'protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>' in Operational mode. For a force to the protection path: 'protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection'. operation-type accepts force, lockout, manual and release; switch-target is not needed for the release and lockout operations. -f forces the command without confirmation. Equivalently the group attribute can be driven with 'set protection-group-<name> pg-request forced-to-protection'; pg-request accepts clear, manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise only for bidirectional SNCP), and defaults to clear.

Use 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> [AID] [transport-entity] [state] [role] [alarm-report-control] [label]' in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The state attribute tells you which unit is carrying traffic: it takes active, standby, available or unknown. The role attribute tells you which side of the pair the unit is, working or protection. So the unit whose state is active is the one currently carrying the traffic, and comparing state against role tells you whether you are running on working or on protection. At group level, 'show protection-group-<name> pg-state' and last-switch-trigger give the corresponding group view and the reason for the last switchover.

Most alarms have both an automatic raise criteria and an automatic clear criteria. A very small subset has no clear criteria and instead requires the user to acknowledge and clear them manually. Find which ones with 'show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true'; only entries with can-be-cleared-by-user = true qualify. Clear them with 'clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*]' in Operational mode, for example 'clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL'. -f forces the command without confirmation. This mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource but with the system itself, that is system wide or global alarms. Anything else will clear only when its underlying condition goes away.

That is controlled system wide by the alarm-control arc-behavior attribute: 'set alarm-control arc-behavior <leave-alarms|clear-alarms>' (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). leave-alarms, the default, means that when ARC is set to 'inhibit' the current alarms are left in a raised mode; clear-alarms means that when ARC is set to 'inhibit' the current alarms are cleared. Check the setting with 'show alarm-control'. The same command carries alarm-soaking-behavior, which takes automatic (soaking time as defined in the FM profile) or no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile get no soaking time), defaulting to automatic; the OSC LOF alarm instead uses the per-facility user-configurable lof-soak-timer on the PBAx card. Alarms suppressed by ARC can still be seen through 'get-conditions'.

Use 'show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type>', for example 'show alarm-inventory-TIM' or 'show alarm-inventory-MSIM' (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). The alarm-inventory holds all possible alarm types for the system with the static information for each. The attributes returned are alarm-type-description, a description of the alarm type (string 0..128); corrective-action, system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered the alarm (string 0..256); alarm-category, one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security; default-severity, the list of possible default severities for that alarm type (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event), which can differ by resource-type; resource-type; and service-affecting, which is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa, since the same alarm may be both sa and nsa depending on the resource-type.

Yes, that is exactly what alarm-severity-entry is for: it configures the severity for one particular alarm, keyed by resource type. Use 'set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>', for example 'set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor' or 'set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major'. severity accepts critical, event, major, minor, not-reported and warning. resource-type is the card or entity type such as CHM1R, FAN or 1830 GX G31; alarm-type is the abbreviated code such as ADMIN-LOCK or BERSD; direction is na, ingress or egress; location is na, near-end or far-end. Read it back with 'show alarm-severity-entry-...', which also returns the read-only service-affecting value (indeterminate, sa, nsa, sa-nsa). Press ? after 'set alarm-severity-entity' to list the available entities. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

alarm-severity-profile assigns a severity to a whole named profile entry rather than to a single resource-type/alarm-type/direction/location tuple. Its syntax is 'set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>', with 'show alarm-severity-profile' to display it; press ? after 'set alarm-severity-profile' to list the available profiles. The profile-entry is itself named after the entry it covers, as in 'set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical'. By contrast 'set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>' changes one individual entry, and only that entry, and its show form additionally exposes service-affecting. Both take the same six severity values, both run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, and both objects are system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

'show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]' gives exactly that, in Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. number-of-alarms is the number of currently raised alarms, and last-changed is the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, counting either a raise or a clear event. Plain 'show current-alarms' returns both. For a per-severity breakdown alongside other system information, the System dashboard from 'status' (or 'status system') prints a line such as '13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor)'. To list the alarms themselves rather than the count, use 'show alarms'.

Look at the conditions with 'get-conditions' (Operational mode). A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as 'not-reported' or 'not-alarmed', when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. The syntax is 'get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]'. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and also defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID are free strings with no default. So filter by alarm-type or AID to find the specific alarm you expected.

Use set-alarm-state, which changes the operator state of an alarm and can store user data in the alarm itself. Syntax: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). The state parameter is mandatory and takes operator-state values 'none', 'ack' or 'close'. Target either all currently raised alarms with all-alarms, or a specific set with alarm-id-list, which accepts from 1 up to 10 alarm ids. acknowledge-text is optional and is a string of length 0..256 that is stored in the alarm. Access mode is Operational Mode. Setting an alarm to the state it already holds is accepted, with only the text updated. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example, or set-alarm-state ack 28872914984089790,17580406225060810165.

Yes. The clear statistics command clears the event counters (statistics) for the specified objects. Syntax: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*. The target parameter is an instance-identifier naming the objects whose event counter statistics are cleared; it accepts a comma-separated list. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation and -h displays help. Access mode is Operational Mode. Scope is limited: the only supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Clear all AAA servers with: clear statistics aaa-server. Clear one server with: clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer.

Use show log with the -n and -t flags: show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. For the security log, show -n=20 -t log security gives the last 20 entries in table display, where columns are aligned instead of the default CSV format in which each column is named in the header. If the aligned table is too wide, drop columns by referencing them after the logname with exclude=<column>; use <tab> auto-complete to list the removable columns. logname values include messages, linecard, shell-command, netconf-command, apps, cli-command, alarm, configuration, kernel, user, event, security and ztp. Results can be post-processed with piped commands, for example show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Note that due to system restrictions the security log may not be cleared.

Yes, that is expected: console logging is off by default. The log-console command controls it, and the enabled parameter, which switches console logging on and off, takes true or false with a default of false. Turn it on with: set log-console enabled true. Syntax is set log-console [source-facilities <value>] [enabled <value>] and show log-console [source-facilities] [enabled]. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The source-facilities parameter takes the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration: all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1 through local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level and uucp. Check current settings with show log-console.

Add a log-console-facility-filter, a selector that filters messages by source facility and severity. Syntax: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]; set, show and delete use the same key. The <name> identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all'. severity takes emergency (level 0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, and defaults to equals-or-higher. To show only serious messages: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical', or use severity error compare-op equals-or-higher to keep error, critical, alert and emergency. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

It is governed by two log-file parameters. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes, a uint8 in the range 1..30, defaulting to 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, a uint8 in the range 1..20, defaulting to 10; when rotating files because max size was reached, the oldest files are discarded if the total number of files exceeds number-of-files. So by default a log keeps 10 files of up to 30 MB, and the configurable ceiling is 20 files of 30 MB. Set them with add log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>] ... or set log-file-<name> .... The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted. Locally saved log files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete.

Yes. Restrict the file's source-facilities to the authentication facility, which carries authentication/authorization attempts messages (syslog facility number 4). Use add log-file-<name> source-facilities authentication, for example add log-file-authonly source-facilities authentication. source-facilities is the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration and defaults to all, so you must set it explicitly. name is a string of length 0...128 characters, without the .log extension. You can then narrow by severity with add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where the filter name is a single facility or 'all', severity defaults to informational and compare-op defaults to equals-or-higher, for example add log-file-facility-filter-authonly/authentication severity warning compare-op equals-or-higher.

Configure the collector with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... transport <udp|tls|tcp> port <value>. Unless you say otherwise, port defaults to 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format defaults to rfc5424 (the alternative is rfc3164). transport defaults to udp, so for TLS you must set transport tls explicitly. Other relevant defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual, source-facilities all, sensitive-data none, destination-facility-override disabled (facility number range 0..11 | 16..23), alarm-report-control allowed. name is a string of length 0...64 and address takes an IPv4, IPv6 or DNS domain name. Example: add log-server-1 address '10.220.225.165' source-facilities local7. Note that syslog remote-logging-switch must be true for any remote destination to be active.

Yes, per collector, but it can only narrow, never widen. The log-server-facility-filter commands filter log messages based on their source facilities and severities, and the filter is based on the source-facilities leaf-list: it can only add a filter to the facilities already configured on that log-server. Syntax: add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], with matching set, show and delete forms. The filter name identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them with 'all'. severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug and defaults to informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals and defaults to equals-or-higher. Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug.

Use the global switch on the syslog container: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. This flag enables remote logging, and when false it disables all remote logging destinations, leaving the configured log-server entries intact. It takes true or false and defaults to true. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode; check the current value with show syslog remote-logging-switch. A separate flag, log-relay, enables remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller and defaults to false. Other syslog attributes include source-address (default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (default true), assignment-method (both, manual or dhcp, default both), niap-compliant-logging (default false), privacy-mode (default false), alarm-report-control (default allowed) and label (string 0..256).

The maximum length of shared-secret is 64 characters; any value longer than 64 characters is denied with an error message. The parameter table types shared-secret as String (length 0...128), with a default value of sharedkey, so treat 64 as the enforced ceiling. The shared secret is displayed as * when read back. Set it on add or set: add aaa-server-<server-name> protocol-supported <value> server-address <value> ... [shared-secret <value>] ..., or set aaa-server-<server-name> shared-secret <value>. The server-name is a string of length 1...64. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

No, that is documented behaviour. For the authentication-requests counter shown by show aaa-statistics-<server-name>, the guide states that for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP, and the authentication requests counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. The aaa-statistics command is only for AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol. Available counters are connection-failures (which includes failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts), authentication-requests, authentication-rejects, authorization-requests, authorization-rejects and accounting-requests, all integers. Example: show aaa-statistics-tacacs_server1. Reset them with clear statistics aaa-server-<name>.

The action parameter of an ACE takes drop, accept or reject and defaults to drop, so an unspecified match is dropped. direction defaults to input (or output), protocol defaults to any, ttl defaults to 255 (range 1...255), logging-action defaults to false, and the source/destination lower and upper ports default to 0. Limits: sequence-id ranges 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and it is recommended to use multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; a further such ACE beyond 16 returns an error. Pre-condition: an ACL must be in place before an ACE can be added, and at least one of source IP, destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. Example: add ace-TrafficV6/100 action drop source-ip-address 2420::5.

Attach an ACL at creation with add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The interface parameter references the interface the filter is applied to, and the available values are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B; use add acl-name interface ? to list them. Yes, IPv6 is handled: type indicates the top-level type of ACL, meaning which fields of the associated IPv4 or IPv6 headers it matches on, and takes IPv4 or IPv6. name is a string of length 0...30, and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock, defaulting to unlock. An ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4.

Yes: show access-control-list. That is the whole syntax; the command is used to show the access control list and takes no parameters. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For per-list detail, use show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface], and for individual entries use show ace-<name>/<sequence-id> with the attributes you want. Note that this is the packet-filter ACL family; the NACM-style authorization rules are separate and are viewed with show access-rule-list-<name> and show access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name>.

Create an access-rule with action deny inside an access-rule-list that is bound to that group. First bind the list: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. Then: add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification, RPC or descendant, or an external command, max 255 characters, default *. operation is a bits value of create, read, update, delete and execute, defaulting to *; write access means create, update and delete. Example: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

Ordering is by sequence-id: the access-rule-list is processed in order as given by the sequence-id parameter, and lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins. sequence-id is a uint16 and can be changed over the lifetime of the list to re-sort entries; if not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, placing the entry at the end of the list. The same sequence-id rule applies to individual access-rules within a list. Bind groups with the user-group parameter of add/set access-rule-list-<name>: a leaf-list of user-group names, defaulting to '*', which is a match-all meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups. A maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. description is a string of length 0..256 characters.

It is OSPF-specific: auth-key adds, edits, shows or deletes an authorization key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The AID makes the scope explicit: add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> key <value> [type <value>]. instance-id is the OSPF instance ID, a number in the range 0..255; ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID; ospf-if-name references the interface in the OSPF area; and spi is a unique security parameter index for the security association, a number in the range 256..4294967295. key is the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection, a string of length 8..128, and type indicates whether the integrity key is ASCII or hexadecimal encoded, taking ascii or hex. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only and then make the fallback defaults deny: set authorization mode rules-only, followed by set authorization read-default deny, set authorization write-default deny and set authorization exec-default deny. In rules-only mode only user defined access-rules are used; the system tries to identify a user configured access-rule first, and if none is found the global defaults read-default, write-default and exec-default apply. Those three are only configurable when mode = rules-only. Their defaults are permit for read-default (get/show and notifications), deny for write-default (create/update/delete), and permit for exec-default (RPC invocation). The other mode values are static-only and static+rules, the default.

A user changes their own password with the password command: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the current/old and the new password are required, and this is supported only for local users. A password may contain up to 200 characters. Run password with no arguments for interactive input, which prompts for the old password and the new password twice and does not echo; Ctrl+C cancels. Inline form: password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!. Inline, the special characters \" and ' must be escaped with \, and #?|; must be enclosed in single or double quotes. Access mode is Operational mode. To reset another user's password, an administrator uses set user-<username> force-password-change true, which forces that user to change their password at next login.

show security. That command displays the top level security container, and it is the complete syntax; it takes no parameters. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the policy flags underneath it, use show security-policies with the attributes you want, for example show security-policies minimum-password-length password-history-size secure-mode. Related show commands in the same area are show access-control-list, show authorization, show user-data and show user-group-<name>.

The configurable minimum is set by minimum-password-length on security-policies: a number in the range 1..200 with a default of 8. It is verified whenever a password is changed. Separately, strict-password-check (true/false, default true) enforces the strict complexity rules: minimum length of 8 characters, at least one lower case letter (a-z), one upper case letter (A-Z), one number (0-9), one symbol, and the user name cannot be part of the password; when disabled only a minimum length of 1 character applies. For history, enforce-password-history-check defaults to true and ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords for that user, and password-history-size, the number of passwords stored for reuse checking, is a number in the range 1..200 with a default of 5. Both policies only affect newly defined passwords once enabled. Set them with set security-policies ...

Both are per-user attributes of the user command. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out); it is a number in the range 0-255 and defaults to 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following consecutive invalid login attempts, expressed in minutes in the range 0 - 1440, defaulting to 5 minutes. Set them with add user-<user-name> [max-invalid-login <value>] [suspension-time <value>] ... or set user-<user-name> .... show user-<user-name> reports user-status, where the value 'lockout' means the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts, and failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login. Lockout can be turned off globally with the disable-user-lockout parameter of security-policies.

show user-data displays the user-data container. That is the entire syntax: the command takes no parameters and no flags. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For per-user attributes use show user-<user-name> with the attributes you want, such as user-group, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, enabled, user-status, force-password-change, max-sessions, last-login-date, failed-logins, user-aaa-type, alarm-report-control and label. For group definitions use show user-group-<name> [description].

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>]. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them. The group name is a String of 1...64 characters, and description, the long description of the user group, is a String of 1...128 characters. Matching commands are set user-group-<name> [description <value>], show user-group-<name> [description] and delete user-group-<name>. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add user-group-XY. show user-group lists the built-in groups: EA Encryption Administrator, MA Monitoring Access, NA Network Administrator, NE Network Engineer, PR Provisioning, SA Security Administrator and TT Turn-up and Test. Attach rules to the group with add access-rule-list-<name> user-group <group>.

Add/Drop Groups are managed with add/set/show/delete adg-<adg-number>. The adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], matching oadm-capabilities max-adgs of 110, so a node supports up to 110 ADGs. Duplicate wavelengths are governed by the read-only show attribute wavelength-duplication, which has two values: one-per-adg (no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and one-per-degree (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). The default is one-per-adg, and only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other attributes: label (String 0..256), max-add-drop-ports (show, integer) and bands-supported, default standardC-band.

On set amplifier-<name>, gain-target is used for constant-gain mode and takes 0..40 dB, default 0.0; it applies only when control-mode is manual. control-mode is auto-max-pw (default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual, and amp-control-support says whether auto-max-pw is even permitted (auto, or manual-only). In auto mode you bias the system value with gain-adjustment, range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, supported only on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: auto (default, system controls tilt from configured fiber parameters), auto-planned (per planning tool parameters) or manual; when the amplifier function is add or drop, only manual is possible. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies in manual mode and raises a traffic-affecting warning; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the auto/auto-planned target, and tilt-actual reports the measured tilt.

Use set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>. The range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different from auto; in control-mode auto the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (default, you configure only span attributes), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes) and manual (even the amplifier target pump powers must be configured). Pump count is read from show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps, whose values are 4 or 2; that value dictates how many pump-power objects the system exposes. Related read-only values are total-pump-power ([-99..99 dBm], -99 means no power), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain.

Turn it on with set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled, for example set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled. ase-idler-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled; enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled. The entity can also be created or removed with add/delete ase-idler-service-<name>, and add/set accept alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). To see whether it came up, read the show-only ase-idler-state: ase-enabled (filling complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (idler signal faulted) or ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed). oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and function (idler) are also shown.

On set ase-idler-source-<name>, target-output-power is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured; its range is (-3.00..20.50) dBm and the default is 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable takes enabled or disabled with default disabled, and the read-only pump-state (enabled/disabled) also defaults to disabled. Example from the guide: set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00'. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). function is fixed at ase-idler-source and oper-state defaults to disabled.

Use the calibrate command, which runs in Operational Mode only: calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type has one value, raman, which triggers calibration on raman cards. trigger is start (starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span) or stop (stops it). entity is an instance-identifier selecting the object to calibrate; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. To start: calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. To stop: calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. There is no default for any of the three parameters.

Degrees are created with add degree-<degree-number>, where degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees; oadm-capabilities reports max-degrees of 20. Spectral granularity is read from show degree-<degree-number>: slot-width-granularity is the width of a slot, default 6250 (value in MHz), and center-freq-granularity is the granularity of allowed center frequencies, default 3125 MHz, computed from a base frequency of 193.1 THz per G.694.1. A media channel is built from between min-slots (default 8) and max-slots (default 32) slots joined together. Other show attributes are is-foadm (default false), wss-less (default true) and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

The pairing is automatic. Direction n and direction n+1 are assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. DWDM Line1 is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even one. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1, 2 when it is dwdm-line2, so odd indexes carry direction-number 1 and even indexes direction-number 2. It also fills direction-card as card-<chassis>-<slot>. The same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Syntax: add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]; delete [-f] forces without confirmation.

The dsc facility supports add/delete/set/show dsc-<name>. The user-configurable attributes are just three: label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited). Everything else is read-only on show: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. managed-by describes whether this facility was system created or not; its values are system (the default) and user. It matters operationally because only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reporting managed-by system cannot be removed with delete.

On add/set dsc-group-<name> the pre-FEC pair is pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, which raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm; setting 0 disables threshold-crossing alarming, and the usable sub-range is per carrier use-case. Its companion pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. The post-FEC pair is post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 12.5..18.0 dB, default 18, raising POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, and post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. A related degrade threshold is dgd-high-threshold, uint16 in the range 25..400 ps, default 100, which raises the DGD-OORH alarm.

Use the gadt command (Golden Application Description Table): show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]. It retrieves information about golden carrier application information, and the four parameters are each a detailed description of an application ID (H, P, S and U), all of type string with no default. It runs in both Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For example, show gadt application-description-H returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application IDs shown here are the same ones that appear in the application field of a golden carrier mode.

gapt lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table. The syntax is show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. It is scoped per card type: card-type is a string, so the table instances appear as gapt-CHM6, gapt-CHM7, gapt-CHM7T and so on, and a bare show gapt lists them with their version and applicable-resource-type columns. version is a string of length 0..5 (for example 1.8 or 3.0) and applicable-resource-type is a string naming the managed resource type(s) applicable for that advanced parameter. Scoping to one card, for example show gapt-chm7, lists that card's entries as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<name>, such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/NLC or /RxCDMode.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode: show gcmt [<card-type>] [version], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Its parameters are object (the golden carrier modes, string) and version (the table version, string). To look up one mode, name it directly: show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P. The output lists golden-carrier-mode golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity (Gbps) 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate (GBaud) 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view of one mode, use show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>.

Read the status attribute: show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status. status describes the carrier mode release status and its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, so a mode is fully supported only when status reads supported, and an experimental mode reports experimental. The same status column also appears in show gcmt output. Two related attributes qualify per-subtype maturity: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string 0..32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The command also returns actual-carrier-mode, capacity, client-mode (ethernet or ethernet-otn), baud-rate, application, compatibility-id and sop-tracking-mode.

The l0-capabilities command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply show l0-capabilities, it takes no parameters at all, and it is available in both Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the OADM-specific limits underneath it, use show oadm-capabilities, which reports max-degrees (20) and max-adgs (110), and for per-degree spectrum granularity use show degree-<degree-number> (slot-width-granularity, center-freq-granularity, min-slots, max-slots, bands-supported).

A Media Channel is created with add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]. The three mandatory inputs are parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency; the two frequencies are values in MHz. parent-oms is an instance-identifier that is only set upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. The system derives center-frequency (MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete defaults to disabled; when enabled the system auto-deletes the MC once its associated NMC is deleted, and it is only allowed on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols), always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000'.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command supports show only: show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]. There is no add, set or delete form. The displayed attributes are name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to the parent and children facilities), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs to the card and port that hold the facility), AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, calculated by the system from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. It is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. By contrast the network media channel filler, nmc-f, does allow set of admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Up to four cards. The syntax is add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>], where adg-number is a number in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card being placed in the ADG. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring defaults to true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer. Example: add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6.

Use the modules-degree command: add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. Unlike an ADG, a degree has only one module index: index is 1, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier of the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. The same command supports set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card <value>], show and delete. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode, privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer. Example: add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1.

Use show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier in MHz (uint32). monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00) with default -99, where -99.00 means no power. The command also returns monitored-width, a uint32 in MHz with default 0, which is the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source or destination. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power.

On add nmc-<name>, center-frequency is mandatory and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. The optional width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The guide states the user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and that the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are set at creation (add) and are read back with show; they are not in the set list. The other mandatory creation input is parent-facility, which can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and whose referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. Example: add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies a default allocated bandwidth of 75000 MHz: alloc-bandwidth is a value in MHz units with default 75000, bounded by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency. What is actually in use is reported separately by actual-bandwidth (MHz, default 0) with actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. Yes, it is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, its values are enabled and disabled, and because it is a system created attribute it is enabled by default. Powers are reported by power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, both [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99, plus output-attenuation-compensation-actual (decimal64, 2 fraction digits, range -20..20, default 0). Only admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable via set nmc-f-<name>.

Use show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8). Either reads 0 if not supported: degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for ILA node-type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. Sample output shows max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. These match the degree-number range [1..20] and adg-number range [1..110].

On set oc-<name>, loopback takes facility, terminal or none, defaulting to none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal with no default. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, defaulting to none. test-signal-direction has the single value ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Example: set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. The list of ochm facilities in an NE will be empty when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored, as configured by the user, or there is no OSC messaging information. The command is set/show ochm-<name>, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode; only label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) are settable. direction reports ingress or egress but only egress is currently supported, and for egress power-actual should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output at the same reference point where the target power is defined. power-actual of -99 dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card) or no power is detected. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99) and attenuation-actual (0..55 dB) apply to HSC OLS nodes.

Use the ocm-channel facility, which lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). Syntax: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. The instance key is name (String, length 0..64) plus lower-frequency and upper-frequency, both uint32, which bound the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point). opm-pwr is the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 in range -99.00..99.00, default -99. connected yields true if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon; values true or false, default false. ocm-channel is show-only, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On ocm-mp the ocm-enable attribute, which enables regular power monitoring, takes values disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Change it with set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable <value>; the only other settable attributes are label (String 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only companions: monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (default enabled); monitored-port, the port actually being monitored, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM (default not-applicable); and ad-direction, the reference to the AD coupler/splitter DWDM port, value ingress. managed-by defaults to system. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility provides dedicated OCM monitoring and is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG. It is not on out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled or disabled) defaults to disabled, so enable it explicitly, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Other settables are label and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only: monitoring-state, default disabled, reported enabled only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible; ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress); last-measurement, the last OCM scan date and time, default never; and adg-number, uint8 in range 0..110, default 0.

On the oms facility grid-mode defaults to flexible, which allows creating and deleting MCs of different widths. The fixed alternatives are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (50 GHz with 88 C-band channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. The default spectrum is standard C-band: lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (191.3 to 196.15 THz). monitoring-mode selects how the OMS is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive, no OCM/DGE), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization (with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization. Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port belonging to a degree, or on node-type ILA.

The ops (Optical Physical Section) facility takes: set ops-<name> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [input-psd-profile] [role] [port-expansion]. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role defaults to general-purpose and may be tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier. port-expansion is no (default) or y-cable, intended for Y-cable expansion. admin-state is lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock; alarm-report-control is allowed (default) or inhibited. supported-roles is read-only and shows which roles the card, and sometimes card-mode, actually permits. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency, type Frequency with overall range 0 or 191275000..196125000 MHz, default 0 (zero means not configured); the usable sub-range and step depend on the module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000 to 196725000 MHz in 50 MHz steps, CHM6 191333000 to 196117000 MHz, CHM2TX 191292500 to 196137500 MHz in 1 MHz steps. Yes, you can trim it: frequency-offset is int16 in range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0, used for bright tuning; once set the frequency changes slowly over 1 to 10 s without affecting service. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, Number in range -55.0..55.00 dBm with accuracy adjustable in 0.5 dBm steps, the real range being pluggable-dependent, for example CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0) and CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2).

Yes, with optical-carrier propagate-shutdown. When it is set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, a Number in range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card. Set both with set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer <ms>.

Very little: the optical-channel facility only supports set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]. label is a user defined String of length 0..256; admin-state is lock, unlock or maintenance with default unlock, for example set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock. Everything else is show-only: name (String 0..64), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs to equipment/card and equipment/card/port), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to parent and child facilities), AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled or disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Read the laser with show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state. It is show-only, values disabled or enabled, default disabled, and reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state; for RD amplifiers it means the source (Tx) pump, and it is only of relevance for DWDM line ports. Yes, you can add fixed pad on receive: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. The Tx counterpart fix-tx-attenuation has the same 0..30 dB range and default 0 but is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured powers are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx, -99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm.

On optical-switch the Signal Fail decision uses working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold, which define the SF threshold for the Working and Protection paths in dBm. Both are settable, range -55.0 to 0 dBm, default -23 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, same -55.0 to 0 dBm range, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only happens when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). facility-los-threshold sets the facility port threshold below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Hysteresis: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF) defaults to 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD) to 2 dB, each 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. osc-control is auto (default) or manual; auto has been supported since R6.0.1, and HSC OLS nodes support auto only. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, na (default) or -2.5..4.5 dBm. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated Tx target, na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the Rx VOA target for manual mode, 0..30 dB, default 10. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6; ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. lof-soak-timer is short (default, about 3 ms) or long (adds 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms) and is only visible on the PBAx card. Read-only: osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx/tx.

Use show otdr-<name> otdr-state. It indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification. Values: not-available (default, status not available), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) and fail (measurement failed). When it fails, otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error. While running, otdr-measurement-time shows the time remaining in the current measurement (integer, default 0), otdr-measurement-port shows the OTDR port under test with 0 meaning the card is not measuring any port, otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available, tx or rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long or raman-precheck1/2/3. otdr-laser-state reports not-available, enabled or disabled.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range sets the distance range in km used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto (default) or 0...300.0 km, and should be the actual fibre length plus 10 percent; from R9.1, if the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, it is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-measurement-speed is auto (default), fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (3 to 5 minutes) or high-precision (5 to 7 minutes). otdr-ior is auto or 1.0...2.0, peak-power auto or 5...14.5, and launching-fiber-length 0...50 m, default 0, with auto not supported.

On the ots facility. Declare fibre with fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both defaulting to SSMF, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor (rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Length is fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto (default) or 0..500.0 km, required for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss is span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 0..80 dB (receive also accepts 99, meaning not configured), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Extra pad goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx, 0..30 dB, default 0. span-loss-reference selects configured or measured (default measured), and span-loss-aging-margin-rx is 0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning; you never create it. The format is ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>, so an RD20TM DWDM line gives show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line, and a C2ILASGH with two lines gives ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. Only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled by default; when enabled a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm, and disabling it clears the alarm immediately and stops the comparison) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters). tx-operator is defaulted by the system to <ne-name>-D00, and rx-operator, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 by default) and tti-port-id are show-only.

ots-r assumes SSMF: required-fiber-type-rx, the required fibre type on the DWDM Line with reference to the Rx fibre, defaults to SSMF and accepts AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor. It is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection. You can also declare fiber-length-rx (unspecified by default, or 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (default 99), external-attenuation-rx, and delta-pointloss, the additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, not-applicable (default) or -1..3.5 dB. target-power-setting is manual or auto, default auto. Show-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and it does depend on that. The ots-r-auto-otdr attribute automatic-otdr enables or disables OTDR based automatic fiber check; its default is enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. It also defaults to enabled if the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with an integrated OTDR, and is disabled if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling while a test is running aborts it and releases the amplifier that the automatic OTDR had blocked; if none is running, no further tests are triggered until re-enabled. Progress shows in auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail or aborted. loss-calibration-by-otdr is none (green field), rx-only, tx-only or tx-rx.

Create it with add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [label] [activation-mode] [auto-delete] [activation-request-fwd] [activation-request-bwd] [direction] [target-output-power-src] [target-output-power-dst] [circuit-id], for example add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. direction is two-way (default) or one-way. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated automatically by the system on creation and deactivated on deletion, and it is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation. In SLTE mode the default is manual and in HSC OLS mode activate-on-create, both controlled through activation-request-fwd/bwd (no-request, activate, deactivate). target-output-power-src and -dst are -18.00..15.00 dBm.

Only on RD20TM, and only when it is operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul; profile-control applies to no other card. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>], access Operational Mode only. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power. direction is tx or rx, but for power-profile only tx is supported. For card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. Attenuation profile-data is <StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...: for OMS values are 0 to 25.50 dB and N is 776 for standard C-band at 6.25 GHz; for NMC values are -10 to 25.50 and N cannot exceed 32.

Almost nothing optical. set pump-<name> only accepts label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed, default, or inhibited). Every other pump attribute is show-only: name, supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. To change pump power you need the separate pump-power command, set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>. Access for pump is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>, where pump-id is the integer number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm and applies when control-mode is manual; the range is -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (the default), with 0 used for the not-applicable case. On an RPBM card the value must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value falls outside the operating range of the Raman sled the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. Read the allowed limits with show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power, each decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows what is programmed in hardware, derived automatically if control-mode is auto, and actual-pump-power shows the measured value, default -99.

Use show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state, for example show raman-calibration-1-8. It reports the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (default, calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale because of OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) and fail (ended with a failure). last-calibration-timestamp gives when the last calibration rpc completed, with or without errors, as date-and-time or never (default never). When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info (string, 0..1024) carries troubleshooting information. Also available: intermediate-results, gain-calibration-error (residual gain error per iteration, in dB) and calibrated-delta-pointloss (-3..3.5 dB).

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. It reports the pilot tone power in both directions: rsc-power-rx is the received Pilot Tone integrated power and rsc-power-tx is the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power, both show-only. Syntax: set rsc-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>], and show rsc-<name> adds supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, label, admin-state, oper-state, avail-state, managed-by, alarm-report-control, rsc-power-rx and rsc-power-tx. admin-state is Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown, default Unlocked; oper-state is enabled or disabled, default enabled; alarm-report control is Allowed (default) or Inhibited; managed-by defaults to system. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the OMS beneath it is not in a monitoring mode that creates one. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer, OMS, has monitoring-mode configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of the managed object depends entirely on the OMS monitoring-mode. The object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Once present it exposes attenuation-setting, a unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum in the range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw, plus the read-only dge-in-use, which reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization.

Use spectrum-control, whose key is name plus direction plus center-frequency: set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>], for example set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1. direction is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and it is the default. center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer or equivalent is in use (dge-in-use = true). target-output-power is not-specified (default) or -55..55 dBm. show adds width (detected width in MHz, 0 if no match or no DGE fibre-connected) and attenuation-actual.

Use the read-only spectrum-monitoring command: show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]. direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice centre in MHz, managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99, where -99dBm means either the power has not yet been measured (the OCM on the DGE2 card measures it) or no power was detected / no appropriate fiber-connection; in the egress direction it is calibrated at the DWDM line port output, the same reference point as the target power. target-actual-power is the ATPS-calculated target, default -99dBm, relevant only when target-power-setting = auto. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz to 2-digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on the spectral width. Example: show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750

Read the contention-check-status attribute of the super-channel. It is accepted on add super-channel-<name> and returned by show super-channel-<name>. Values are pending, success, overridden and failk, with pending as the default. The state is set via DNA in openwave mode, and it is only applicable if openwave-contention-check is enabled at the super-channel-group level. openwave-contention-check is the attribute that enables the DNA-assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode; its values are false and true and it defaults to false, so if you never enabled it on the parent SCG the contention-check-status stays at pending and tells you nothing. line-system-mode on both the super-channel and the super-channel-group defaults to openwave.

-m is the merge flag: it merges configuration so the command will not fail if the entity already exists.
